purpose: Functional MPTCP continuity on existing shared-DAX Firecracker guest, including actual L1 A-to-B state-only snapshot handoff

network.transport: virtio-net single-queue TAP/vhost-net over an isolated host Linux bridge

configuration.moving_endpoint: MPTCP client in L2; fixed peer/listener in L1 B

findings.timing_interpretation: Single functional handoff uses serial control and 512-character state-transfer chunks, includes a 50ms ingress quiet period. The peer clock observes wall-clock blackout; the paused guest clock can exclude suspension time. These values are not optimized CXL mailbox/direct-handoff or MPTCP steady-state performance.
findings.destination_dax_ram_log: 2026-10-22T07:49:13.259805500 [anonymous-instance:main] DAX_RAM path=/dev/dax0.0 offset=2097152 gpa=0 bytes=134217728 initialize=false hva=0x7f4623000000

limitations: One coherent physical host with QEMU-emulated shared CXL; no physical multi-host or noncoherent/DMA/flush correctness proof.
Snapshot restores fresh destination KVM/vCPU/EPT. Direct and reuse paths still reject network devices and require additional device/backend handoff implementation.
Moving endpoint is client. Moving server/inbound connections need ADD_ADDR delivery and remote path-manager participation; current block-old-path-first procedure does not cover them.
No shared host CXL packet staging queue; pending old-path packets may be lost and recovered by MPTCP/TCP.
50ms source-ingress quiet is controlled lab quiescence, not a general NIC/backend drain guarantee.
Echo records are not a bulk-throughput benchmark; no steady-state CPU or throughput percentage is inferred.
Destination guest and fixed peer share L1 B after handoff, so pre/post RTT paths differ.
